FREN 101.title: Beginners' French I
FREN 101.description: Basic vocabulary, the rudiments of grammar and familiarization with cultures of the French-speaking world. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Not for credit for students who completed Core French 11, 12 and/or French Immersion (BC Curriculum or equivalent).

FREN 102.title: Beginners' French II
FREN 102.description: A continuation of FREN_V 101. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Not for credit for students who completed Core French 11, 12 and/or French Immersion (BC Curriculum or equivalent). This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 101. Credits will be granted for only one of FREN_V 102 or FREN_V 103.

FREN 103.title: Intensive Beginners' French
FREN 103.description: Fundamentals of the French language. Aligned with CEFR level A1. This course is recommended for students who are not complete beginners in French.

FREN 201.title: Elementary French I
FREN 201.description: Continued improvement in listening, speaking, reading and writing. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of Core French 11, FREN_V 102, FREN_V 103 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 202.title: Elementary French II
FREN 202.description: A continuation of FREN_V 201. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 201 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 301.title: Intermediate French I
FREN 301.description: Refinement of reading, writing and speaking skills through the study of contemporary literature and other authentic documents of the French-speaking world. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of Core French 12, FREN_V 202 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 302.title: Intermediate French II
FREN 302.description: A continuation of FREN _V 301. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 301 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 311.title: Introduction to Literature in French
FREN 311.description: Critical reading of foundational literary texts in French from genres of prose fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and theatre. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 302 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 321.title: Critical Writing
FREN 321.description: Practical tools for university-level writing in French. Apply stylistic devices and rhetorical structures to form questions and arguments, analyse literary and cultural objects, and produce a variety of essay genres. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 302 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 330.title: Introduction to Quebec Literature
FREN 330.description: Survey of representative literary texts from Quebec viewed in their historical, social, and cultural contexts. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

FREN 331.title: Arts, Cultures and Society from the Middle Ages to the Revolution
FREN 331.description: Exploration of early French culture and literature from the Middle Ages to the close of the Early Modern period and the French Revolution; the impact of society on the arts and vice versa. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

FREN 341.title: Arts, Cultures and Society from Romanticism to the Present Day
FREN 341.description: Exploration of modern and contemporary French culture and literature from the early 19th century to the present day; the impact of society on the arts and vice versa. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

FREN 346.title: French at Work
FREN 346.description: Communicative French for students preparing for a career in the francophone world. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 123 or FREN_V 302.

FREN 352.title: French Grammar
FREN 352.description: Principles of grammar theory and contextualized French grammatical concepts. Emphasis on terminology and analysis of grammatical issues. Aligned with CEFR level B2. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 123 or FREN_V 302.

FREN 353.title: Advanced French Grammar
FREN 353.description: Advanced grammar theory and critical analysis of difficult French grammatical structures. Emphasis on autonomous examination of complex grammatical issues. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

FREN 357.title: French to English Translation
FREN 357.description: Principles, practical strategies and methods of translation from French to English. Overview of the main challenges involved in intercultural communication. If your French is stronger than your English, please take FREN_V 457 before FREN_V 357. This course is recommended for students who have taken FREN_V 352, and one of FREN_V 224, FREN_V 401.

FREN 370.title: Introduction to French Linguistics
FREN 370.description: A survey of basic terminology, methods, problems, and theoretical trends in French linguistics, specifically designed to provide students with a foundation for advanced language study in French. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 224 or FREN_V 401.

FREN 395.title: Special Topics Abroad
FREN 395.description: Study of Francophone literature, history, culture, or communities in an authentic context. Topics and locations may vary. Consult Department for current offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed FREN_V 202 or FREN_V 112 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 401.title: Upper-Intermediate French I
FREN 401.description: Communicative proficiency at an autonomous level: vocabulary enrichment, pronunciation practice, grammatical analysis and development of efficient reading and writing techniques. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of French Immersion 12, FREN_V 123 or FREN_V 302 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 402.title: Upper-Intermediate French II
FREN 402.description: A continuation of FREN_V 401. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 401 or assignment based on placement test.

FREN 407.title: Medieval French Literature
FREN 407.description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of French-language literature of the Middle Ages (11th-15th centuries) in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite.

FREN 408.title: Renaissance: Studies in 16th-century French Literature
FREN 408.description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of sixteenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 409.title: Ancients and Moderns: Studies in 17th-century French Literature
FREN 409.description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of seventeenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 410.title: Enlightenment and Revolution: Studies in 18th-century French Literature
FREN 410.description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of eighteenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 413.title: Tradition and Modernity: Studies in 19th-century French Literature
FREN 413.description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of nineteenth-century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 414.title: The Modern and Contemporary French Novel
FREN 414.description: Major historical, social and artistic movements reflected in representative novels published in France from the 19th Century to the present. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 415.title: French Digital Culture
FREN 415.description: Contemporary issues and debates on how media and digital technologies have impacted French culture and society. Examines how text, language, and writing are used in digital media. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 416.title: Contemporary French Literature and Culture
FREN 416.description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of twentieth- and twenty-first century French literature in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 417.title: Popular Fiction
FREN 417.description: Popular genres in modern French fiction, including science fiction, crime, romance, fantasy and historical fiction. Aesthetic characteristics, historical context and cultural relevance. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 418.title: African and Caribbean Francophone Literatures
FREN 418.description: Representative and contemporary writings from African and Caribbean francophone cultures. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 419.title: Women's Writing
FREN 419.description: Representative women's writings from the Middle Ages to the present; contemporary women's writings in the Francophone world. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 420.title: Selected Topics in French Literature and Culture
FREN 420.description: Study of a literary or cultural topic that extends beyond one chronological period and/or place proper. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 427.title: French Cinema
FREN 427.description: Study of major past and contemporary French film productions. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 428.title: Francophone Cinema
FREN 428.description: Study of major past and contemporary film productions from around the Francophone world.

FREN 430.title: Quebec Literature and Culture
FREN 430.description: Study of representative aspects of Quebec literature and culture through the study of literary texts, films, and artistic productions in their historical context. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 431.title: Indigenous Literatures of Francophone Canada
FREN 431.description: Study of the literature and cinema of First Nations, Inuit and Métis creators working in French and in Francophone spaces in Canada. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 440.title: Francophonie: History and Current Debates
FREN 440.description: Historical origins, cultural and linguistic paradoxes of Francophonie. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 441.title: Francophone Literatures and Cultures of North America
FREN 441.description: Forms of French language cultural expression in North America in their historical context. Discussion of issues around minority linguistic and cultural rights. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 442.title: Cultures of the Francophone World
FREN 442.description: Forms of cultural expression of the Francophone world studied in their context. Regions may include the Americas, Africa, East Asia, Europe, Indian Ocean, Middle East, and/or the Pacific. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 443.title: Postcolonial Studies
FREN 443.description: Interdisciplinary approaches to Postcolonial Studies through francophone literature and theory. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 450.title: Old French
FREN 450.description: The phonetics, grammar, and vocabulary of major Old French dialects; corpus of various literary texts. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 451.title: French Phonetics
FREN 451.description: Theory and practice of the sound system of the French language. Anatomy of speech production, sound discrimination, phonetic description and transcription. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 455.title: Creative Writing in French
FREN 455.description: Theory, techniques and practice of creative writing in French in a variety of genres. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 457.title: English to French Translation
FREN 457.description: Extensive practice in English-French translation of a wide range of texts and discourses, such as literary, legal, medical, administrative, commercial materials. Analysis of linguistic and cultural problems posed by translation of specialized material. If your French is stronger than your English, please take FREN_V 457 before FREN_V 357. This course is recommended for students who have taken FREN_V 352, FREN_V 357, and one of FREN_V 225, FREN_V 402.

FREN 460.title: History of the French Language
FREN 460.description: Overview of the development of the French language from its Latin roots to its modern forms. Examination of the internal and external factors which brought about changes in its phonology, morphology, syntax and lexis. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 470.title: Studies in Modern French Linguistics
FREN 470.description: Current topics in French linguistics. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 472.title: Morphology and Syntax of the French Language
FREN 472.description: Analytical principles pertaining to the study of words and word-stems (morphology), and phrases and sentences (syntax) in written and spoken French. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 474.title: Lexicology and Semantics of the French Language
FREN 474.description: Study of the vocabulary of modern French, focusing on basic principles in lexical semantics, lexicology, phraseology, lexicography, terminology and new technologies, neology. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 476.title: French Language and Societies
FREN 476.description: Study of language in its social context, covering aspects of sociolinguistics within and across the French-speaking communities of the world. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 477.title: Contemporary Varieties of French
FREN 477.description: Study of the different varieties (or dialects) of contemporary French and issues related to French-speaking communities around the world. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to prerequisite below.

FREN 480.title: French Theory
FREN 480.description: Core ideas of French theorists. Influence of French theory on the social sciences and humanities, focusing on Marxism, feminism, structuralism, deconstruction, postmodernism and postcolonialism. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 484.title: History of the Book
FREN 484.description: A historical approach to the social transformations of the book trade in France. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 485.title: Early Encounters: Travel Literature and Colonial Writing in French
FREN 485.description: Narratives of travel and exploration in French before 1800 and their relationship to colonization, knowledge production and representations of the self and others. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 495.title: Research Seminar in French Literature and Culture
FREN 495.description: Research on critical topics related to French literature and culture. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 496.title: Research Seminar in French Language and Linguistics
FREN 496.description: Research on critical topics related to French language and linguistics. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. This course is recommended for students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402, in addition to the prerequisite below.

FREN 498.title: Directed Reading
FREN 498.description: Focus on a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of the department head and of a supervisory faculty member is required. This course is recommended for the fourth year students who have completed one of FREN_V 225 or FREN_V 402.

FREN 499.title: Honours Essay
FREN 499.description: Restriction: this course is restricted to students in one of these programs: BA in fourth-year with one of these specializations: HON FREN or HON RMST.

FREN 509.title: Studies in the Nineteenth-Century French Novel

FREN 521.title: Studies in Francophone Literatures and Cultures

FREN 556.title: Studies in French Language and Linguistics

FREN 591.title: Proseminar I: Research Skills and Scholarly Practices
